summary:
Scope: the route used to publish Host 0.9.0 (adds Claude transcript provenance on top of 0.8.0), from the cited workflows, scripts and tests. It is process knowledge from one successful publication, not the release contract (see contract/telemetry-host) and not a grant to dispatch.

Shape: a candidate workflow builds and verifies the package once; a publish workflow then runs with publish=true, pins to the live Authority main, writes a publication journal through the Authority repo's journal writer (all eight effects verified) and publishes the tag, the GitHub release, nuget.org and the org feed. Each real dispatch is an admitted effect.

Lessons: (1) the publisher preflight refuses when Authority main moved before genesis. A burst of settlement-bot commits on the Authority repo caused one such refusal; it occurred before anything was written, so nothing needed rollback, and the retry was one further admitted dispatch that succeeded. Ask for a quiet window rather than a retry loop. (2) Irreversible once published: the tag, the journal generation, the release assets and the org feed version; nuget.org can only be unlisted. A defect means the next version and journal, not an edit. (3) nuget.org adds a signature file to the package, so archive equality is false there by design; the producer payload equality is the criterion, and the release package and org-feed package should be byte-identical. (4) The org feed answers 401 to an anonymous reader, so an independent read needs the observation workflow with its token: pins in scripts/telemetry-host-published-org-read.py (tag, release id, asset ids, content ids) must be updated to the new version by a normal source PR before that workflow can verify it, and the workflow does not accept the publication (publicationAccepted stays false). Until then the org feed is Unknown from outside, and the publisher's own journal observation is the only evidence. (5) The new release is not marked latest by this route.
title: Publishing a Host successor is two dispatches with an Authority journal; the org feed needs a workflow-token read and separate observer pins
